notes_list.title: Resonance / Mesomeric Effect
notes_list.basic_overview: Delocalization of electrons through conjugated p orbitals stabilizes molecules, ions and transition states when valid resonance contributors can be drawn.
notes_list.extra_info_content: +M groups donate lone-pair electron density into a pi system; −M groups withdraw electron density. Resonance contributors are not rapidly interconverting structures; the real species is a resonance hybrid.
notes_list.examples: Phenoxide vs alkoxide: phenoxide gains resonance stabilization. Aniline lone pair is delocalized into the ring, reducing basicity relative to aliphatic amines.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Conjugation requires suitable geometry/orbital overlap; twisting can reduce overlap. Solvent and protonation state can switch which resonance form is relevant.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Ensure continuous p-orbital overlap. 2. Move only electrons, not atoms. 3. Preserve octets where possible. 4. Compare major contributors by charge separation, octets and electronegativity.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Resonance stabilization lowers the energy of the species and can lower activation barriers when the transition state is similarly stabilized.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Predict aromatic substitution effects, acidity/basicity, radical and carbocation stability.
notes_list.common_traps: Never move a sigma bond to create a resonance contributor; never exceed second-row octets.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
